mainEntity.name: How much does a cubic yard of mulch cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: One cubic yard (27 cubic feet) covers about 162 square feet at 2 inches deep, 108 square feet at 3 inches, and 324 square feet at 1 inch.
Two to three inches is typical for flower and shrub beds. Use about one inch when refreshing existing mulch. Very deep layers can hold too much moisture against plant stems.

mainEntity.name: Is bulk or bagged mulch cheaper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bulk is usually cheaper per cubic foot once you need more than about a cubic yard, but you must collect it or pay for delivery. Enter your local prices above to compare the two.
Fresh mulch and compost compress and break down. Adding 5% to 10% means the bed is still at the right depth after it settles.

mainEntity.name: Will a pickup truck carry a cubic yard?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes for light mulch, but soil and stone are heavy. A full yard of topsoil or gravel can be well over a ton, so check your truck's payload rating.
